name: Stone Lion of Ifrane
hero_subtitle: The carved stone lion that has become the symbol of Morocco’s alpine-style Middle Atlas town.

overview.title: The town’s postcard symbol
overview.p1: The Stone Lion sits in central Ifrane and appears on countless photos of the town. It is a short stop rather than a full outing — ideal when you arrive or before heading to the lakes and cedars.
overview.p2: Combine with a café in the centre and a stroll past the chalet-style architecture that earned Ifrane its Little Switzerland nickname.

food.title: Eating near the lion
food.p1: Cafés and simple restaurants sit within a short walk of the town centre and the stone lion.
food.p2: Use the lion as a meeting point, then eat in central Ifrane — not at the monument itself.
food.li1: Centre cafés for coffee and pastries.
food.li4: Stock snacks before forest or lake outings.
food.li5: Mountain evenings can be cold — prefer indoor seating.

faq.title: FAQ about Stone Lion of Ifrane

q1.question: Is it worth a special trip?
q1.answer: Yes as part of seeing the town — not a half-day site on its own.

q2.question: How old is the lion?
q2.answer: A modern town symbol linked to Ifrane’s planned resort identity.

q5.question: Far from the lakes?
q5.answer: The lakes need a short drive; the lion is in town.
